headline: Founding, running, and
other adventures.
hero.lead: Thanks for stopping by. Here’s my background and what I’m currently building, thinking about, and exploring.

work.heading: Ideas should be the constraint, not the available technology.
paragraphs: My north star throughout my career has been working to improve people’s lives and the world at scale, especially through new technology. I am relentlessly curious and love learning and solving creative, complex problems.

At CodeYam, I am working to make it possible for more people to build beautifully designed, highly maintainable software with AI. For non-technical people and vibe coders, that means being able to build good software at all. For developers and teams, it means moving faster and working better together.

We built, launched, scaled, and iterated on several products, and that R&D led to our breakthrough: CodeYam Editor. It installs as a Claude Desktop integration or runs from the command line, connects to the AI agents you already work with, and generates software simulation. The workflows around it are built to make both the person and the agent better at creating and changing software. I co-founded the company and am in the product nearly every day.

about.heading: How I got here
paragraphs: Before becoming a founder, I spent my career building and launching new products at Lyft, where I was a founding member of the Bikes & Scooters team and helped take a new business from zero to millions of riders. I was also on the team behind the award-winning redesign of the rider app . My role scaled from a generalist product marketing IC to acting head of marketing for the line of business, running a 30-person org across product marketing, growth, and local marketing, and then back to an IC as product lead for transit, bike, and scooter payments, where we shipped Lyft’s first transit payment integration. I am oriented toward impact and solving the hardest problems for the business and its users, which results in a non-linear journey I would not change.

I currently serve as Director of Growth on the Board of Harvard Alumni in Tech. I was a South Park Commons Founder Fellow in the inaugural 2021 cohort and an Alliance DAO alum from cohort nine. I graduated from Harvard College, where I was an NCAA Division I fencer. Now based in New York City, I enjoy running and surfing nearby.

adventures.heading: The places I go and the things I do outside of work
paragraphs: I’ve always been active. My first love was soccer as a kid, though I multitasked and experimented (hello basketball, softball, horseback riding, guitar, photography, baking, writing). I dreamed of surfing, which I finally learned when I moved to San Francisco. I dabbled in running there (Bay to Breakers, twice) before getting more deeply into the roads and trails in Colorado and now NYC. I picked up yoga, bouldering, and snowboarding along the way. I’m now content being a fast, serious reader and a slow, fun runner.
I started fencing the summer before high school and quickly ended up a nationally and world-ranked junior fencer. Harvard recruited me for their NCAA Division I team, where I was a four-year starter.

A Californian at heart, but after nearly a decade on the West Coast it was time to move back east. I’m newly in New York City, after three years in Denver. Favorites over the years: safari and hiking in South Africa, surfing in Costa Rica, Mexico, Cornwall, and Bali, and time in Cairo, Sydney, and New Zealand. I also get out for as many semi-local adventures as I can: Salida for the hill climb and FIBArk, Rockaway Beach from New York, Steamboat Springs and the Front Range from Denver.
